facts.text: Madama Butterfly premiered at La Scala on 17 February 1904 in a two-act version, and was withdrawn after a disastrous first night.
evidence: had its premiere on 17 February 1904 at La Scala in Milan
was withdrawn after a disastrous premiere

facts.text: At the 1904 premiere, audience plants were given nightingale whistles for the sunrise. The audience took it as a cue to make animal noises of their own.
evidence: give audience plants nightingale whistles to deepen the sense of sunrise in the final scene
The audience took the noise as a cue to make their own animal noises.

facts.text: The premiere was called “one of the most terrible flops in the history of Italian opera”. One problem: no intermission in the very long second act.
evidence: one of the most terrible flops in the history of Italian opera
the lack of an intermission during the second act

facts.text: Puccini’s sister Ramelde wrote that night: “The second act I didn’t hear at all, and before the opera was over, we ran out of the theater.”
facts.attribution: Ramelde Puccini, letter to her husband, 1904 (via Wikipedia)
facts.evidence: The second act I didn't hear at all, and before the opera was over, we ran out of the theater.

facts.text: Puccini rewrote it, splitting the long second act in two. The new version was a great success in Brescia on 28 May 1904.
evidence: splitting the second act in two
This second version (SC 74.B) was performed on 28 May 1904 in Brescia, where it was a great success

facts.text: The Humming Chorus became the bridge between Puccini’s new Acts II and III.
facts.evidence: with the Humming Chorus as a bridge to what became Act III

facts.text: There are five versions of Butterfly. Puccini’s final 1907 revision, the “Standard Version”, is the one usually performed.
facts.evidence: which has become known as the "Standard Version" and is the one that is most often performed today

facts.text: Butterfly reached the Metropolitan Opera on 11 February 1907, in Puccini’s third version.
facts.evidence: which was performed at the Metropolitan Opera in New York on 11 February 1907

facts.text: The first US performances, in 1906, were in English, by Henry Savage’s touring company.
facts.evidence: the first US performance was presented in English on 15 October 1906, in Washington, D.C.

facts.text: From the long love duet that closes Act I: “Bimba dagli occhi pieni di malia”, “Sweetheart, with eyes full of enchantment”.
facts.evidence: Bimba dagli occhi pieni di malia ("Sweetheart, with eyes full of enchantment")

facts.text: Sharpless brings a letter from Pinkerton asking him to break the news that he isn’t coming back to Japan.
facts.evidence: Pinkerton is not coming back to Japan

facts.text: “Il cannone del porto!”, the cannon at the harbor, leads into the famous Flower Duet.
facts.evidence: Il cannone del porto! ("The cannon at the harbor!", often known as The Flower Duet).

facts.text: The musical Miss Saigon (1989) was inspired by Madama Butterfly.
facts.evidence: Miss Saigon, a musical by Claude-Michel Schönberg and Alain Boublil, is inspired by the opera
